decisions.statement: Every address handed in is restated over one reading of the bodies.
A spelling is found by the parse rather than by matching the text of the body.
A body is parsed only where its text spells the page type of an address.
A body spelling no address handed in is read and left alone.
The bodies read are the ones a search of the tree names.
The bodies read are the paths the world holds once the edits so far have landed.
A path the answer writes is read beside the paths the index lists.
A path the answer carries away is left out of the bodies read.
A tree that could not be searched refuses rather than restating nothing.
An address is a page type and a slug parted by `/`, with a scope between them.
An address handed in that is no address refuses the whole answer.
An address handed in as its own new address refuses the whole answer.
A call handing in no address at all is refused.
A slug naming a page without its page type is left as that slug is.

definition: the edits restating many pages' addresses over one reading of the bodies
